doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Mongo Santamaria and early recording sessions
title: The February 1966 Atlantic session with Latin influence
summary: Brown lists personnel on an Atlantic session; Laws notes the Latin influence from playing with Mongo.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I’m showing another session. This – they list this by session as well as – so I’m not sure. Maybe the chronology’s a little strange here. But there’s one that’s – it’s on Atlantic, February 24, 1966. It’s Bloodshot, Mean Lean, No, You’d Better Not, and then Home Folks, which was unissued as well. On this date, Chick and Rodgers Grant. Chick is only on the first one, Bloodshot, and there’s Ray Lucas playing drums.
That’s right. He played on No, You’d Better Not, and also Martin Banks, the trumpet player, played a trumpet solo on that.
Right. He’s on there. Garnett Brown on trombone, Benny Powell, Jimmy Owens, Chris White on bass, Carmelo Garcia, Victor Pantoya. So still in the Latin – a lot of the Latin influence.
Right. That was a strong influence, coming from playing with Mongo’s band.
